tailDefinition: ceil(N/100) slowest actual client all-three RTT (replicas-start); deterministic sequence tie break
limits: This is the profiled diagnostic run. JFR, ByteBuddy callbacks and event commits alter scheduling/load; never mix this TPS/p99 into unprofiled capacity comparisons.
Per-phase CPU is not measured. Pipeline stages are wall time; service callback product duration is same-JVM nanoTime.
Commit release remains its native entry/exit bracket, never an invented exact timestamp. Negative elapsed lower bounds indicate overlapping brackets, not clamped zero.
Cross-recording estimates convert each JVM nanoTime using its own JFR offset envelope and assume the common Docker VM wall clock. Raw nanoTime values from different JVMs are never subtracted.
One client anchor proves an observed offset bracket at the anchor, not arbitrary drift absence throughout the run; node callbacks additionally require a common offset intersection.
Follower ACK wait includes reception, durability, reporting, leader polling and scheduling, not pure network latency.
FileForce is nested inside ArchiveBlock on the same thread; nested durations must not be added to parent stages.
Stages from different members run in parallel and nested/overlapping stages must not be added into a critical-path total.

GC overlap uses same-recording GCPhasePause unions only; overlap is temporal coincidence, not proof that GC caused the entire stage. Per-request overlaps share pauses and must not be summed across requests.
No individual follower marker receive times are present. Latest product end to all-three observation is a cohort-end estimate, not each follower transport latency.
